{'[0]': '[0] Earlier reports had suggested that Apple was planning to launch a 20th-anniversary edition iPhone next year, featuring an all-glass chassis design. However, analysts at the investment bank Jefferies believe that the device will no longer move forward.'}

{'[1]': '[1] Wall Street analysts say the major redesign plan for the 20th-anniversary iPhone has been shelved.'}

{'[2]': '[2] Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple\'s stock rating to "Underperform" today. Analyst Edison Lee pointed out that the possible cancellation of the 20th-anniversary iPhone\'s major redesign is one of the main reasons for this downgrade.'}

{'[3]': '[3] The key to this downgrade lies in news that Apple\'s all-glass iPhone project has been cancelled. Although rumours about the project being in development surfaced as early as 2025, with some expecting a 2027 launch, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple quietly filed a patent for an "all-glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered an all-glass iPhone to be reasonable and credible, but Edison Lee believes development has stalled. The analyst noted that supply-chain checks showed the project was terminated due to poor yield rates. Edison Lee believes that, with memory costs soaring, this decision is a "major blow" to driving high-end iPhone sales. He estimates that, had the device launched on schedule in September 2027 to celebrate the iPhone\'s 20th anniversary, its average retail price would have reached US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any model in history. Edison Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, thereby further raising the average selling price and gross margins." He believes that, with memory prices rising, this should have been an important defensive strategy.'}

{'[4]': "[4] Edison Lee also pointed out that Apple's artificial intelligence strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are other reasons for this stock downgrade."}

{'[5]': "[5] Based on Edison Lee's report, it remains unclear whether the analyst is referring to the entire redesign plan being shelved, or only some design elements being abandoned."}

{'[6]': '[6] The most-liked comment was posted by Currentinterest.'}

{'[7]': '[7] These analysts have been wrong too many times in their predictions about Apple\'s future plans. Even the concept of an "all-glass" design has never accurately reflected Apple\'s true intentions. The 20th-anniversary phone will be unique and creative, and whatever the final design turns out to be, it will be very well received.'}

{'[8]': '[8] For example, reports circulating for months have pointed out that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an all-glass display is simply not possible. However, the rumoured quad-curved bezel design may still be achievable.'}

{'[9]': '[9] Regardless, if the redesign of the 20th-anniversary iPhone has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets should soon confirm it.'}
